source.title_on_document: Central Tendency Bias in Human Selection of AI-Generated Design Variations

paper_design_summary: Fifty participants recruited through university mailing lists selected among high- and low-variance sets of manually constructed posters in a within-person experiment; stimulus-set order was randomized within each task and task-block order was counterbalanced (PDF pp. 2-3, III.B-D). Participants selected their preferred design and a design representing each set, and the analysis compared participant-level center-selection rates (PDF pp. 3-4, III.E, Table I and IV.B-C). The study provided no generative-AI assistance and scored no participant-produced creative output (PDF p. 2, III.B; p. 3, III.D-E; p. 5, V, limitations).

assignment.what_was_assigned: The order of high- and low-variance poster sets was randomized separately for each participant within each selection task. All participants experienced both variance conditions. Task-block order was counterbalanced, but random allocation to the counterbalancing sequences is not stated. This randomization concerns stimulus presentation, not generative-AI assistance: the posters were manually constructed (PDF p. 2, III.B; p. 3, III.D).
assignment.quote: Within each block, the order of stimulus sets was randomized for each participant to prevent sequence effects.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 3, III.D Procedure; PDF p. 2, III.B Method

arms.name: High-variance design sets
arms.description: Manually constructed posters spanning a broad stylistic continuum. Within-person condition: the same 50 people also completed the low-variance condition; these are overlapping counts, not separate groups (PDF p. 2, III.B; p. 3, III.D and Table I note).

arms.name: Low-variance design sets
arms.description: Manually constructed posters clustered near the perceptual centroid. Within-person condition: the same 50 people also completed the high-variance condition; these are overlapping counts, not separate groups (PDF p. 2, III.B; p. 3, III.D and Table I note).

participants.who: Participants recruited through university mailing lists, with varied design training; student/professional status is not stated. Table I explicitly identifies 50 participants in the analyzed trial totals. The paper does not separately report a participant count at randomization.
participants.quote: Percentages are aggregated across trials (50 participants × 8 sets per condition = 400 trials).
participants.locator: PDF p. 3, III.C Participants and Table I note; III.D Procedure establishes exposure to both conditions

ai_tool.name_model: None; no generative-AI model used in the experiment
ai_tool.how_used: The researchers manually constructed poster stimuli to control stylistic variance. Grid presentation approximated image-generation interfaces; Midjourney and DALL-E are examples discussed, not tools used in the study (PDF p. 2, III.B Method; p. 5, V, limitations).

task.description: Design selection, without producing a creative artifact: choose the most-liked poster and the poster best representing the overall style of a set. Each participant viewed the same 16 sets in both tasks, with 8 sets per variance condition and 8 posters per set (PDF p. 3, III.D-E).
task.duration: No time limit imposed (PDF p. 3, III.D Procedure).

contrasts.reported: High variance: 56% (224/400 trials); low variance: 34% (136/400 trials); paired-samples t(49) = 3.51, p = 0.001. Percentages are aggregated across trials; the test uses participant-level center-selection rates.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 3, Table I and note, IV.B Preference task; III.E Measures

contrasts.reported: High variance: 66% (264/400 trials); low variance: 38% (152/400 trials); paired-samples t(49) = 4.34, p < 0.001. Percentages are aggregated across trials; the test uses participant-level center-selection rates.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 3, Table I and note, III.E Measures; PDF p. 4, IV.C Representativeness task

eligibility.reason: Criterion 1 is not met because no generative-AI assistance was assigned: stimuli were manually constructed (PDF p. 2, III.B; p. 5, V, limitations). Within-person stimulus-set order was explicitly randomized (PDF p. 3, III.D), so assignment.randomized is yes for presentation order, but this is not random assignment of AI. Criterion 2 is met: Table I explicitly reports 50 participants in the analyzed trial totals, with the same people in both variance conditions (PDF p. 3, III.D and Table I note). Criterion 3 is not met: the outcomes are center-selection rates in preference and representativeness judgments of supplied posters, not creativity or diversity scored on participant-produced output (PDF p. 3, III.D-E and Table I; p. 4, IV.C). This perceptual-choice experiment is coded other and fits none of the codebook context classes.

one_line_finding: Among 50 participants selecting manually constructed posters, high- versus low-variance sets increased center selections from 34% to 56% for preference (t(49) = 3.51, p = 0.001) and from 38% to 66% for representativeness (t(49) = 4.34, p < 0.001); no generative-AI assistance was tested (PDF p. 3, Table I; p. 2, III.B).
